title: Translating KV Caches Between Hybrid-Attention Language Models: MLA Latents, Linear-Attention States and Sparse-Attention Indexers
summary: The method replaces full-context re-prefill when one model takes over another model's conversation, mapping the source model's KV cache (MLA latents, linear-attention states, sparse-attention indexer keys) into the target's format via token-wise linear maps, closed-form corrections, or recurrence replay. The cost is building and validating per-pair translators, including decoding token ids from layer-0 latents for long-range recall, which adds engineering complexity beyond standard serving stacks. It can fail through degraded recall without token-identity recovery, inherited source behaviors (6% refusals), collapse under naive re-translation in multi-turn transfer, and unverified generalization to 300B+ models.
rationale: The technique targets mid-scale open-weights hybrid models (16-48B) and requires per-model-pair translator engineering with evaluation infrastructure that exceeds what a small team with one 24 GB GPU can adopt or validate today.
